request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a "watched due" total for the signed-in user, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

The change is only in `src/main/frontend/features/header/SheetHeader.tsx`; the server and stored data didn't need touching. It uses the list of people the user watches, which the app already loads, and adds up each person's due-total the same way the crew total does:
- People whose due-total shows as n/a are skipped.
- Watching no one gives `0.00`.
- The figure appears as `watched-due-total`, after the reviews count.

Starting or stopping a watch already refreshes that list, so the total updates straight away without reloading the sheet.
